central_question: Does a source-independent nocturnal arthropod assemblage on Madeira Island, sampled across native Laurissilva, mixed and exotic forest plots, show the same endemic-native and introduced-altered forest association observed in the separate three-island Azorean SLAM forest study?

new_source.original_arthropod_guild_dominance: Lepidoptera 76.2% of published occurrences; different SLAM arthropod detection channel
new_source.published_source_prior_art: 2026 original authors already report Madeira moths endemic/native/introduced composition, e.g. 63 endemic/68 non-endemic native/38 introduced/10 migratory among 179 moth taxa; this is prior art, not fresh Structural discovery.

If any required original source metadata or habitat support missing, terminal for this replicated habitat question. No retrospective replacement with dry-vs-native forests, all sites, Lepidoptera-only threshold, guessed origin codes or source phenology.

v329_source_opaque_limits.strict_source_schema_habitat_and_origin: At least one declared explicit forest-habitat candidate in source Event and an origin term in Occurrence, plus core/foreign keys, otherwise do not open source Event values

scientific_ceiling: At most one genuinely different archipelago and island (Madeira); external field survey independent source but not independent 3-island macroecological replication.

Night light traps attract mobile moths from beyond source habitat, so trap-caught species may not inhabit exact plot. Original paper focuses artificial light at night; potential confounding with forest type.
Two source trap methods cannot be pooled by counts or capture rates, nor compared numerically to Azores SLAM interception trapping.
Forest habitat is not randomized; elevation, disturbance, ALAN, season and geography can confound differences.
200 named taxa and 1939 occurrences are not independent replicated forest units; explicit author site IDs and collection campaign frame must be checked.
Any link to SLAM native forest result is independent dataset comparison, not a species-level meta-analysis or evidence of population persistence, immigration or experimental selection.
